approvedReports.title: Weekly situation report · week 40
approvedReports.author: Aline Uwase
approvedReports.summary: Ebola cases in Rubavu are still rising. If nothing changes, the outbreak is likely to keep growing for several weeks, and isolation beds may run short.
keyPoints: Each sick person is currently infecting more than one other person.
Isolation beds at the district hospital are close to full.
Finding and isolating sick people faster makes the biggest difference.

figures.label: Isolation beds needed at the busiest point

recommendations: Fund extra isolation beds in Rubavu now.
Support faster testing so sick people are isolated within 3 days.

approvedReports.title: Effect of faster isolation on Ebola
approvedReports.author: Aline Uwase
approvedReports.summary: Isolating sick people within 3 days instead of 7 lowers the likely number of cases in most scenario runs.
keyPoints: Speed of isolation matters more than any single other action.
Results are estimates, not exact predictions.

figures.label: Cases with isolation within 3 days
figures.range: about half as many as with 7 days

recommendations: Set a national target of isolation within 3 days of symptoms.

approvedReports.title: Marburg: protecting health workers
approvedReports.author: Aline Uwase
approvedReports.summary: In 2024, most Marburg cases in Rwanda were health workers. Giving staff full protection early lowers how many of them are infected.
keyPoints: Health workers face the highest risk early in an outbreak.

figures.label: Share of cases among health workers

recommendations: Keep protective equipment stocked at all referral hospitals.

approvedReports.title: Isolation capacity across Western Province
approvedReports.author: Aline Uwase
approvedReports.summary: Current isolation capacity may not be enough in about 4 in 10 scenario runs.
keyPoints: Opening 8 extra beds lowers this to about 1 in 10 runs.
recommendations: Prepare annex wards that can open within 48 hours.

approvedScenarios.name: Ebola · current response
approvedScenarios.plan: Sick people are isolated after about 4–5 days, half of burials are safe, and some contacts are followed up.

approvedScenarios.name: Ebola · isolate within 3 days
approvedScenarios.plan: Same as today, but sick people are found and isolated within 3 days.

approvedScenarios.name: Ebola · slow response (7 days)
approvedScenarios.plan: Sick people take about a week to be isolated, for example if testing is delayed.

approvedScenarios.name: Ebola · full package
approvedScenarios.plan: Isolation within 3 days, 80% safe burials and most contacts followed up daily.

approvedScenarios.name: Marburg · protect health workers early
approvedScenarios.plan: Hospital staff wear full protection from day 7 instead of day 21.

interventionReviews.name: Isolate sick people within 3 days
interventionReviews.description: Faster testing and transport so people with symptoms are isolated quickly.

interventionReviews.name: Safe and dignified burials
interventionReviews.description: Trained teams handle burials so the virus does not spread at funerals.

interventionReviews.name: Full protection for hospital staff from day one
interventionReviews.description: Gloves, gowns and masks for all ward staff as soon as a case is suspected.

interventionReviews.name: Follow up contacts daily
interventionReviews.description: Teams check every contact of a sick person each day for 21 days.

interventionReviews.name: Extra isolation beds in Rubavu
interventionReviews.description: Open an 8-bed annex ward at Gisenyi District Hospital.
interventionReviews.effectRange: From about 4 in 10 runs to 1 in 10 runs

reportDrafts.title: Ebola in Rubavu: effect of faster isolation
reportDrafts.summary: Scenario estimates suggest isolating sick people within 3 days lowers the median outbreak size. The uncertainty range is wide, so results compare options rather than predict exact numbers.

reportDrafts.title: Marburg: protecting health workers early
reportDrafts.summary: In most runs, the share of cases among health workers falls when full protection starts earlier. Marburg parameters are provisional.

reportDrafts.title: Ebola in Gasabo: isolation bed needs
reportDrafts.summary: Across runs, peak isolation bed demand stays within current capacity in about two thirds of scenarios.
